structure.title: Following the rabbit
structure.text: Alice enters a world in which size, identity, and rules no longer remain dependable between encounters.

structure.title: Encounters and authority
structure.text: Episodic conversations lead towards more public displays of rule-making. The puzzles concern language as often as events.

people.name: Alice
people.text: A seven-year-old who follows a rabbit down a hole and keeps trying to apply schoolroom rules to a world that answers every question with nonsense.

people.name: The White Rabbit
people.text: A nervous, waistcoated rabbit, forever late and checking his watch, whose hurry is what pulls Alice into Wonderland in the first place.

people.name: The Queen of Hearts
people.text: A furious monarch who settles every difficulty by shouting for heads to be cut off, and who runs her croquet ground and her court the same way.

context.title: Nonsense with rules
context.text: Many absurdities depend on applying language or logic too literally. The joke often has a precise mechanism rather than no sense at all.
context.takeaway: Look for the rule that has slipped.

context.title: Lessons and recitations
context.text: Alice's remembered lessons offer a standard she expects to trust. Their failures make education part of the comic material.

notice.text: Notice corrections that change the subject.
notice.why: Authority can be performed without answering a question.
Social rules become hard to obey when others keep rewriting them.

opening: Alice follows a rabbit and finds a world where everyone is ready to correct her, although their rules change whenever she tries to obey them. Her body will not keep a sensible size, conversations turn into traps, and authority becomes more confident as it becomes less reasonable. Carroll gives childhood's experience of being instructed by baffling adults the precision of a logical nightmare. Alice's effort to remain polite and make sense of things supplies the comedy, until politeness starts to look like an unnecessary concession.
